newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat sees car output rising by 2001 - report.
newsitem.headline: Fiat sees car output rising by 2001 - report.

text.p: Fiat Auto expects to maintain a heavy investment program over the next five years and to be producing three million cars a year by 2001, the managing director of the Fiat SpA division told Il Giornale daily.

"Some 1.8 million cars wil be made in Italy and the others in the rest of the world," Roberto Testore was quoted as telling the newspaper. "Already this year we will reach the 2.5 million car mark, thanks to the launch of new models in Europe and the development of the Palio in Brazil," he added.
The Palio is Fiat's recently-launched world car aimed at markets outside Europe.
Testore said that to maintain Fiat's momentum, the company planned investments totalling 20 trillion lire between 1998 and 2002.
"Some 16.5 trillion will be used to renew models and continue the process of modernizing plant; 3.5 trillion lire is earmarked for the development of world markets," he said.
